newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Common Fund to hold annual meeting in Morocco.
newsitem.headline: Common Fund to hold annual meeting in Morocco.

text.p: The Common Fund for Commodities, a U.N. affiliate, said on Wednesday the 8th annual meeting of its governing council would be held in December in Marrakesh, Morocco.
It said the meeting would be attended by delegates from its 104 member countries.
Ivory Coast joined in October and procedures are under way to admit Burma as the 105th member.
The Common Fund said the meeting, scheduled for December 2 and 3, would discuss the Fund's operations under its second account, which finances commodity development projects.

The Fund last month approved eight new projects covering the cocoa, coffee, zinc, cotton and coconut sectors, taking to 50 the total number of projects approved since it became fully operational in 1991.

The Amsterdam-based Fund said it would also review its net-earnings programme, aimed at helping developing countries liberalise their markets through the establishment of functioning commodity market structures.

The programme, which focuses particularly on least developed countries, is aimed at setting up effective controls for private sector commodity trading in countries where trade was previously conducted through state-connected bodies.
In addition it seeks to train local commercial banks in commodities trade financing.
The programme is targeted at the cocoa, coffee and cotton sectors and focuses mainly on African producers, concentrating initially on two or three developing countries per sector on a pilot basis.
The Common Fund said the governing council meeting would be preceded by meetings of regional groups on December 1, including the African Group and Least Developed Countries.
